title: Morphy Richards Trimmer Internal Repair Manual
summary: Morphy Richards trimmer teardown and internal repair guide. This trimmer uses 3 H1 screws in total: 1 visible screw at the back and 2 hidden screws behind the front plastic hood. After removing all screws, both side clips must be unclipped to open the shell. This manual also includes a demo repair playbook for an internal cut or disconnected wire.

locations.details: Single visible screw at the rear of the trimmer body.
Two hidden screws behind the front plastic hood.

notes: Do not attempt to force open the shell before removing all 3 screws.
The two front screws are concealed by a plastic hood and must be exposed first.

locations.release_method: Insert a plastic pry tool into the seam and gently release.
Repeat after partial separation of the shell.

notes: Side clips hold the shell even after all screws are removed.
Aggressive prying may crack the body shell.

teardown.overview: To open the Morphy Richards trimmer shell, first check if the blade head or comb attachment is still on and remove it, then remove the 1 visible rear screw, then remove the front plastic hood to expose 2 hidden front screws, remove those screws, and finally unclip both side seams.

steps.title: Power off and disconnect
steps.instruction: Ensure the trimmer is switched off and disconnected from charging power before starting disassembly.

steps.title: Check and remove blade head
steps.instruction: Look at the top of the trimmer. If the blade head or comb attachment is still attached, remove it first by pulling or sliding it off. The blade head must be removed before accessing housing screws. If no blade head is visible (already removed), skip to the next step.
steps.vision_condition: If blades or comb teeth are visible at the top of the trimmer, the blade head is still attached and must be removed. If the top shows a flat surface or exposed mounting area with no blades, the head is already off.
steps.skip_if: No blade head or comb attachment visible on the trimmer

steps.title: Locate rear screw
steps.instruction: Identify the single visible screw at the back of the trimmer housing.

steps.title: Remove rear screw
steps.instruction: Use an H1 screwdriver to remove the visible rear screw.

steps.title: Lift front plastic hood
steps.instruction: Carefully lift or remove the front plastic hood using a plastic pry tool.

steps.title: Expose hidden screws
steps.instruction: Once the front hood is removed, identify the two hidden front screws.

steps.title: Remove hidden screws
steps.instruction: Use the H1 screwdriver to remove both hidden front screws.

steps.title: Release side clips
steps.instruction: Use a plastic pry tool along the left and right seams to unclip the shell sides.

steps.title: Separate shell halves
steps.instruction: Carefully separate the shell halves once screws and side clips are fully released.

common_errors: Trying to open the shell before removing the 2 hidden front screws.
Using a metal tool that scratches or cracks the front hood.
Forcing the shell apart before unclipping the side latches.

known: Housing is secured by 3 H1 screws and side clips.
Internal wiring is available for visual inspection after the shell is opened.
unknown: Exact battery chemistry and connector type

notes: Battery details for this specific Morphy Richards trimmer variant are not yet confirmed.
replacement_notes: Match voltage, chemistry, dimensions, and polarity.
safety: Do not puncture, crush, or short battery terminals.
Avoid accidental shorting while the shell is open.

notes: Motor and blade drive details are not yet confirmed for this variant.
Blade head may remain assembled unless servicing requires deeper access.
Use caution around sharp cutting edges.
Remove loose hair before deeper inspection.

checks: Check whether the trimmer responds during charging before opening the shell.
Inspect charging contact or port area visually after opening if power fault is suspected.

symptoms: Housing feels stuck after one screw removed.
Rear opens slightly but front remains locked.
Shell flexes but does not separate.
likely_causes: Two hidden screws behind front hood not removed.
recommended_actions: Remove front plastic hood and check for hidden screws.
After all screws are removed, unclip both side seams.
If still dead, open the shell and inspect internal wiring.

possible_internal_causes: Broken wire near battery or motor
troubleshooting.next_step: Open housing and inspect internal wiring for loose or cut wires.

symptoms: One wire end appears detached or broken
likely_causes: Weak prior joint or partial cut
recommended_actions: Inspect both ends of the broken or loose wire.
Temporarily join the wire ends to confirm diagnosis.
If the trimmer powers on, secure the wire ends as a temporary fix.

repair_playbooks.goal: Safely open the trimmer shell without breaking the body.
stop_conditions: Plastic begins whitening or cracking under force.
Shell remains locked after known screws are removed.
Front hood does not release cleanly and may still be latched.
success_signs: Shell halves separate with minimal force.

repair_playbooks.goal: Determine why the trimmer body is still stuck.
likely_causes: One or both hidden front screws are still installed.
Front plastic hood is not fully removed.
A side clip is still engaged.
checks: Confirm the rear screw is removed.
Confirm both front hidden screws are removed.
Inspect both side seams for remaining clip engagement.

repair_playbooks.goal: Identify and temporarily fix a disconnected internal wire to restore power.
symptoms: Loose or visibly broken wire inside housing
likely_causes: Wire cut due to stress or movement
tools_required: optional soldering iron for permanent fix

steps.title: Ensure safe handling
steps.instruction: Make sure the device is not connected to charging power before touching internal wires.

steps.title: Locate the disconnected wire
steps.instruction: Visually inspect internal wiring and identify any loose or cut wire ends.

steps.title: Prepare test connection
steps.instruction: Gently bring the two ends of the disconnected wire close together.

steps.title: Temporary contact test
steps.instruction: Lightly touch or hold the wire ends together to restore connection temporarily.

steps.title: Test device behavior
steps.instruction: Carefully try turning the trimmer on while maintaining contact between the wire ends to check if it starts working.

steps.title: Confirm diagnosis
steps.instruction: If the trimmer powers on, confirm that the disconnected wire is the issue.

steps.title: Temporary wire securing
steps.instruction: Align the wire ends properly and wrap them securely with electrical tape as a temporary fix.

steps.title: Final power test
steps.instruction: Turn on the trimmer again to confirm stable operation after the wire is secured.

steps.title: Prepare for reassembly
steps.instruction: Place the repaired wire so it does not get pinched when the shell is closed.

permanent_fix_recommendation: For long-term reliability, solder the wire connection instead of relying only on tape.
warnings: Never touch exposed wires while the device is connected to charging power.
Avoid letting exposed wire ends touch metal parts or other conductors.
Temporary tape repair may fail over time.
Do not pinch repaired wires during reassembly.
success_signs: Device powers on when the wire ends are joined.
Device continues working after temporary securing.
stop_conditions: Wire insulation is badly burned or damaged.
The trimmer still does not respond after reconnecting the wire.
The repaired wire cannot be positioned safely inside the shell.

repair_playbooks.goal: Close the trimmer safely after inspection or wire repair.
steps: Confirm the repaired wire is routed safely and not crossing a screw post or seam edge.
Press the shell together until side clips engage.
warnings: Do not trap the repaired wire between shell halves.
Make sure the front hood sits properly before the final rear screw check.
success_signs: Trimmer powers on after full reassembly.

hidden_tips.tip: Two important screws are hidden behind the front plastic hood.
The housing is secured by side clips even after all screws are removed.
If the body is not opening, check the front again before applying more force.
If the device is completely dead, internal wire disconnection near the battery, switch, or motor can be a possible fault point.
Before closing the shell, make sure repaired wires are not sitting on top of clip points or screw posts.
If the blade head or comb is still attached, it must be removed before attempting screw removal. Look for blades or comb teeth at the top — if visible, slide or pull off the head first.

warnings: Disconnect charging power before opening the shell.
Use a plastic opening tool to reduce damage risk.
Do not force the shell apart if hidden screws may still be installed.
Do not handle exposed internal wires while the trimmer is connected to charging power.
Avoid accidental shorting during internal inspection.

known_replaceable_areas: blade head or attachments depending on variant

inspection_prompts_for_agent: If the blade head or comb is still attached and blocking access, ask the user to remove it before opening the housing.
Ask the user to show the rear screw location clearly.
Ask the user to show the front plastic hood before prying.
Ask the user to confirm both hidden front screws are removed.
Ask the user to show the side seam while unclipping.
Ask the user to show the loose wire closely from both ends.
Ask the user to hold the wire steady before confirming the temporary join.
Ask the user to show the wire routing before closing the shell.
If the user is using a screwdriver or metal tool near the plastic seam, remind them to use light pressure and avoid cracking clips.

evidence.detail: 1 screw is visible at the back.
2 screws are hidden behind a front plastic hood.
Sides must be unclipped to open the shell.
Manual includes a demo playbook for temporarily joining and taping a cut internal wire to restore function.
